**24 palavras novas** (linguagem especializada).
**Texto do dia:** editorial / opinião.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre economia a partir de um editorial, usando terminologia precisa e nuances de grau.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Editorial: Inflation, Not Inflection
paras: Economists distinguish **inflation**, a sustained rise in prices, from a one-off **price shock**. The distinction matters: central banks that **overreact** to a shock risk **choking off** growth, whereas those that **underreact** to genuine inflation allow expectations to **de-anchor**.

The present data are **ambiguous**. Headline inflation has eased, **yet** core inflation has **proved sticky**. Policymakers would be **ill-advised** to **declare victory**. **Not so much** a crisis **as** a test of nerve.

items.q: The editorial treats price shocks and inflation as identical.

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
rows: **Headline inflation has eased, yet core inflation…**
**Not so much a crisis as a test of nerve.**

blocks.body: **Not so much X as Y** = “menos X do que Y”. Em economia, a precisão do termo (*inflation × price shock*) é o próprio argumento.

items.s: Not ___ much a crisis as a test of nerve. (so)
Headline inflation has eased, ___ core inflation has proved sticky. (yet)
They would be ill-___ to declare victory. (advised)
Economists ___ inflation from a price shock. (distinguish)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Keep a lid on.** — Manter sob controle.
**Tighten the belt.** — Apertar o cinto.
**A drop in the ocean.** — Gota no oceano.
**Rock the boat.** — Agitar as coisas.
**Stay the course.** — Manter o curso.
**Read the signs.** — Interpretar os sinais.
**Ride out the storm.** — Enfrentar a crise.
**Cut both ways.** — Ter dois gumes.
**Smooth sailing.** — Sem problemas.
**Cost an arm and a leg.** — Custar os olhos da cara.
**Is this inflation or a price shock?** — É inflação ou choque de preços?
**Headline has eased, yet core is sticky.** — A cheia recuou, mas o núcleo persiste.
**Should the bank declare victory?** — O banco deve declarar vitória?

items.label: Ajuste refinado de entonação
items.note: Ajuste refinado de entonação: pequenas variações de altura e de ritmo mudam a atitude (cortesia, ironia, reserva, compromisso) sem mudar as palavras.
words: I suppose that’s one way to put it. ↘↗ (reserva)
Well, that’s ONE way to put it. ↘ (ironia)

prompts.model: Inflation is sustained; a shock is one-off.
It is not so much a crisis as a test of nerve.
It would be ill-advised to cut rates yet.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence editorial paragraph on a policy issue using a precise distinction and a not so much… as… contrast.
blocks.model: Economists distinguish a temporary dip in demand from a lasting slowdown. The data are ambiguous: sales have recovered, yet hiring remains weak. Not so much a collapse as a slow leak. Policymakers would be ill-advised to ignore it. Waiting costs less than overreacting, but only up to a point. The test is patience.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
